# Deconvolution algorithms included in the benchmark

::: {.callout-note}
Shared notation: **Y** = $(Y_{gn}) \in \mathbb{R}^{G \times N}$ is the bulk matrix; **X** = $(X_{gj}) \in \mathbb{R}^{G \times J}$ is the single-cell or purified reference matrix; **P** = $(P_{jn}) \in \mathbb{R}^{J \times N}$ is the cell-type proportion matrix. The generic convolution model is
$$
\mathbf{Y} \approx \mathbf{X}\mathbf{P} + \mathbf{E},
\qquad
\mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{p}_n=1,\quad \mathbf{p}_n \geq 0.
$$
:::

See @tbl-deconv-algorithms.

| Algorithm | Full algorithm name | Single-cell reference as prior input | Reference normalization | Deconvolution framework | General category | Bulk normalization | Main pros | Main cons | GitHub / CRAN / web | Last update | Licence | Bibliographic reference |
| --------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ | --------- | --------- | ------------------- | ----------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| **BayesPrism** | **Bayesian cell Proportion Reconstruction Inferred using Statistical Marginalization** | Annotated scRNA-seq counts $$c_{gc}$$ are collapsed into cell-type-specific gene probability vectors: $$\theta_{gj}=\frac{\sum_{c \in j} c_{gc}+\alpha}{\sum_{g'} \sum_{c \in j} c_{g'c}+G\alpha}$$. These $$\theta_{gj}$$ act as priors for cell-type expression; malignant or unknown components can be refined from the bulk. | Counts | Bayesian multinomial mixture: $$\mathbf{y}_n \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}\left(L_n,\sum_j p_{jn}\boldsymbol{\theta}_j\right)$$. Priors are placed on proportions and expression parameters; posterior inference estimates $$\mathbf{p}_n$$, uncertainty and cell-type-specific expression. | Probabilistic / Bayesian | Counts | Full posterior uncertainty; integrates bulk and scRNA-seq; can re-estimate cell-type-specific expression; strong for oncology/TME. | Computationally heavier; needs high-quality reference; more complex priors and workflow. | <https://github.com/Danko-Lab/BayesPrism> | GitHub pushed 2026-04-03 | GPL-3.0 | Chu et al. (2022), *Nature Cancer*, 3, 505--517. DOI: 10.1038/s43018-022-00356-3 |
| **Bisque** | **BisqueRNA: decomposition of bulk expression with single-cell information** | Single cells are averaged by cell type and possibly by subject: $$X_{gj}^{(s)}=\frac{1}{|C_{js}|}\sum_{c \in C_{js}} c_{gc}$$. Bisque learns gene-wise transformations aligning scRNA-seq references with bulk profiles. | Counts | Transformed regression model: $$Y_{gn} \approx \alpha_g+\beta_g\sum_j X_{gj} P_{jn}+\varepsilon_{gn}$$. Fractions are estimated under non-negativity and sum-to-one constraints. | Regression-based | Counts | Robust integration of scRNA-seq and bulk; useful with matched bulk/single-cell information; simple output. | Sensitive to reference quality; CRAN package archived; less robust when platforms are poorly aligned. | <https://github.com/cozygene/bisque>; formerly <https://cran.r-project.org/package=BisqueRNA> | CRAN archived 2025-06-02 | GPL-3 | Jew et al. (2020), *Nature Communications*, 11, 2891. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-020-16607-9 |
| **CIBERSORTx** | **CIBERSORTx: next-generation CIBERSORT for cell abundance and expression purification** | The reference is a signature matrix $$X_{gj}$$ built from purified or single-cell profiles, often restricted to marker genes $$g \in \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{markers}}$$. CIBERSORTx can additionally correct batch/platform effects and impute cell-type-specific expression. | CPM | Robust support-vector regression: $$\widehat{\mathbf{p}}_n=\arg\min_{\mathbf{p}_n \geq 0}\|\mathbf{y}_n-\mathbf{X}\mathbf{p}_n\|_{\varepsilon}+\lambda\|\mathbf{p}_n\|_2^2$$. Uses $$\nu$$-SVR-like regression plus optional batch correction and expression purification. | Regression / machine-learning | TPM | Widely used; robust to correlated signatures; supports batch correction and cell-state/expression imputation. | Web/closed service; non-commercial restrictions; less transparent; signature matrix quality is critical. | <https://cibersortx.stanford.edu/> | Web service; current code update not exposed | Free for non-commercial use | Newman et al. (2015), *Nature Methods*, 12, 453--457; CIBERSORTx extension DOI: 10.1038/s41587-019-0114-2 |
| **DWLS** | **Dampened Weighted Least Squares** | Marker genes and average cell-type profiles are derived from scRNA-seq: $$X_{gj}=\frac{1}{|C_j|}\sum_{c \in C_j} c_{gc}$$. Weights emphasise informative genes and dampen dominance by abundant cell types. | Counts | Weighted constrained least squares: $$\widehat{\mathbf{p}}_n=\arg\min_{\mathbf{p}_n \geq 0}\sum_g w_g(Y_{gn}-\sum_j X_{gj} P_{jn})^2$$ subject to $$\mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{p}_n=1$$. | Regression-based | TPM | Strong for rare cell types; efficient; interpretable; good benchmark performance. | Marker selection matters; assumes linear mixtures; reference-dependent. | <https://bitbucket.org/yuanlab/dwls/src/master/> | Public Bitbucket date not reliably exposed | GPL | Tsoucas et al. (2019), *Nature Communications*, 10, 2975. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-019-10802-z |
| **MuSiC** | **Multi-subject Single-Cell deconvolution** | Uses subject-specific single-cell references: $$X_{gj}^{(s)}=\frac{1}{|C_{js}|}\sum_{c \in C_{js}} c_{gc}$$. Cross-subject means and variances are estimated so unstable genes receive lower weight. | Counts | Weighted NNLS: $$\widehat{\mathbf{p}}_n=\arg\min_{\mathbf{p}_n \geq 0,\, \mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{p}_n=1}\sum_g w_g(Y_{gn}-\sum_j X_{gj} P_{jn})^2$$. Weights reflect residual and cross-subject variability. | Regression-based | TPM | Handles multi-subject references; robust to individual variability; interpretable weighted regression. | Needs multi-subject reference; related cell types may be hard to separate; normalization matters. | <https://github.com/xuranw/MuSiC> | README update 2024-01-15 | GPL $$\geq$$ 3 | Wang et al. (2019), *Nature Communications*, 10, 380. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x |
| **SCDC** | **Single-Cell Deconvolution by multiple single-cell RNA-seq references** | Multiple references $$\mathbf{X}^{(r)}$$ are used. Each reference gives a base estimate: $$\widehat{\mathbf{p}}_n^{(r)}=\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{y}_n,\mathbf{X}^{(r)})$$. The method combines references to reduce reference-specific bias. | Counts | Ensemble estimator: $$\widehat{\mathbf{p}}_n=\sum_r \omega_r \widehat{\mathbf{p}}_n^{(r)}$$ with $$\omega_r \geq 0$$ and $$\sum_r \omega_r=1$$. References closer to bulk data receive higher weights. | Ensemblist | TPM | Integrates multiple references; reduces batch/reference dependence; useful with public scRNA-seq atlases. | Depends on base methods; reference quality still matters; license metadata appears ambiguous. | <https://github.com/meichendong/SCDC> | GitHub activity visible in 2025 issues; code-update date not reliably exposed | MIT in supplied table; GitHub metadata ambiguous | Dong et al. (2020), *Briefings in Bioinformatics*. DOI: 10.1093/bib/bbz166 |

Training minimises prediction loss: $$\min_{\theta}\sum_m \|\mathbf{p}^{(m)}-f_{\theta}(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}^{(m)})\|^2$$. | Deep learning | TPM | Captures nonlinear patterns; fast once trained; can be robust to noisy or complex signatures. | Less interpretable; requires simulation/training; domain shift between simulated and real bulk can reduce accuracy. | <https://github.com/KevinMenden/scaden> | v1.0.0 release 2021-06-09 | MIT | Menden et al. # Phenotype-guided single-cell approaches

::: {.callout-note}
Shared notation used across the table:

$$
Y_i \in \{0,1\}, \qquad i=1,\ldots,n
$$

where $Y_i=1$ denotes the positive bulk-level phenotype, for example successful trunk-like gastruloid differentiation, and $Y_i=0$ denotes failed differentiation with neuroectodermal output.

$$
X^{\mathrm{bulk}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\hat{G}\times n},
\qquad
X^{\mathrm{sc}} \in \mathbb{R}^{G\times K}
$$

where $\hat{G}$ is the set of genes shared between bulk and single-cell data, $n$ is the number of bulk samples, and $K$ is the number of single-cell profiles.

$$
A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times K}
$$

is the bulk-to-single-cell similarity or correlation matrix, with entry $A_{ik}$ measuring the similarity between bulk sample $i$ and single cell $k$.

$$
\eta=(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_K)^\top
$$

is the cell-association coefficient vector. A positive coefficient indicates a cell positively associated with $Y=1$, a negative coefficient indicates inverse association, and a zero coefficient indicates weak or no association. Unless otherwise stated, $\lambda$ denotes an $L_1$-type sparsity penalty.
:::



| Algorithm | Expected single-cell normalization | Expected bulk normalization | Supported phenotype types | Output type | Theoretical framework, short description | Core objective / score in shared notation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Scissor** | Seurat-style normalized and scaled expression after QC; commonly log-normalized counts restricted to genes shared with bulk. | Preprocessed bulk expression matrix with samples matched to phenotype labels; genes aligned to scRNA-seq. | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous` | **Positive / Negative / Neutral** | Network-regularized regression. First computes bulk–cell similarity $A$, then fits phenotype $Y$ using sparse cell coefficients while encouraging similar cells to receive similar coefficients. | $$\hat{\eta}=\arg\min_{\eta}\mathcal{L}(Y,A\eta)+\lambda\left[\alpha\|\eta\|_1+(1-\alpha)\eta^\top L_{\mathrm{cell}}\eta\right]$$ $\eta_k>0 \Rightarrow$ Positive; $\eta_k<0 \Rightarrow$ Negative; $\eta_k\approx0 \Rightarrow$ Neutral. |
| **DEGAS** | Single-cell expression transformed into model-ready input; often normalized expression with optional phenotype column for cells if available. | Bulk expression transformed into the deep transfer-learning input space; matched to phenotype labels. | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous` | **Positive / Other** after thresholding | Deep multitask transfer learning with domain adaptation. Learns latent representations of bulk and single-cell profiles and transfers disease or phenotype impressions from bulk samples to cells. | $$\min_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}\{Y,f_\theta(X^{\mathrm{bulk}})\}+\gamma\,\mathrm{MMD}\{h_\theta(X^{\mathrm{bulk}}),h_\theta(X^{\mathrm{sc}})\}+\Omega(\theta)$$ Cells receive continuous phenotype-impression scores; thresholding gives Positive versus Other. |
| **scAB** | Normalized single-cell expression; used to construct bulk–cell similarity and cell graph terms. | Preprocessed bulk expression matrix matched to clinical or binary phenotype labels. | `binary`, `survival` | **Positive / Other** | Knowledge- and graph-guided non-negative matrix factorization. Decomposes bulk–cell similarity into latent factors regularized by phenotype and cell–cell similarity. | $$\min_{W,H\ge0}\|A-WH\|_F^2+\alpha\,\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{pheno}}(H,Y)+\alpha_2\,\mathrm{tr}(HL_{\mathrm{cell}}H^\top)$$ High phenotype-associated factor scores are mapped to Positive; remaining cells are Other. |
| **LP_SGL** | Single-cell data are normalized and clustered; Leiden communities define cell groups. | Preprocessed bulk expression matrix matched to phenotype vector or survival data. | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous` | **Positive / Negative / Neutral** | Sparse group lasso with community structure. Uses Leiden-derived cell groups to impose both cell-level sparsity and group-level sparsity. | $$\hat{\eta}=\arg\min_{\eta}\mathcal{L}(Y,A\eta)+\lambda\left[(1-\alpha)\sum_g\sqrt{p_g}\|\eta_g\|_2+\alpha\|\eta\|_1\right]$$ Groups $g$ are Leiden communities; selected positive and negative coefficients define cell classes. |


| Algorithm | Expected single-cell normalization | Expected bulk normalization | Supported phenotype types | Output type | Theoretical framework, short description | Core objective / score in shared notation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SCIPAC** | Normalized single-cell matrix; highly variable genes, PCA, clustering and optional batch correction are used. | Preprocessed bulk expression projected into the same reduced feature space or used to estimate phenotype coefficients. | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous` | **Positive / Negative / Neutral** | Quantitative association estimation. Clusters cells, fits elastic-net regression on bulk data, and maps bulk-derived coefficients back to single-cell profiles to estimate cell–phenotype association strength. | $$\hat{\beta}=\arg\min_{\beta}\mathcal{L}(Y,Z^{\mathrm{bulk}}\beta)+\lambda\left[\alpha_{\mathrm{EN}}\|\beta\|_1+\frac{1-\alpha_{\mathrm{EN}}}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2\right]$$ $$s_k=(z^{\mathrm{sc}}_k)^\top\hat{\beta}$$ Bootstrap-derived intervals or p-values classify cells. |
| **PIPET** | Optional log-normalization and scaling before similarity matching; may filter genes by cell detection frequency. | Bulk expression used for differential expression and phenotype-specific feature-vector construction. | `binary`, `continuous` | **Positive / Negative / Neutral** in SigBridgeR harmonization | Phenotype-guided similarity matching. Constructs phenotype feature vectors from bulk-derived DEGs and scores each cell by similarity to phenotype-associated templates. | Define marker/template vector $m_+$ for $Y=1$ and $m_-$ for $Y=0$. $$s_k=d(x^{\mathrm{sc}}_k,m_-)-d(x^{\mathrm{sc}}_k,m_+)$$ Large positive $s_k$ indicates Positive association; negative values indicate inverse association. |
| **scPAS** | Normalized single-cell expression; selects features and derives gene–gene similarity network from scRNA-seq or bulk. | Preprocessed bulk expression matrix matched to phenotype labels. | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous` | **Positive / Negative / Neutral** | Network-regularized sparse regression with permutation testing. Similar to sparse regression on $A$, but explicitly regularizes gene or cell network structure and estimates significance through permutation. | $$\hat{\eta}=\arg\min_{\eta}\mathcal{L}(Y,A\eta)+\lambda\|\eta\|_1+\rho\,\eta^\top L_{\mathrm{network}}\eta$$ Permutation-derived null distributions provide p-values or FDR-controlled cell labels. |
| **scPP** | Normalized single-cell expression ranked per cell; AUCell-style ranking is used for marker enrichment. | Bulk data used to identify phenotype-associated marker genes by differential expression or association testing. | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous` | **Positive / Negative / Neutral** | Marker projection via AUCell enrichment. Finds phenotype-associated markers in bulk and evaluates whether each cell ranks those markers highly. | For marker set $M_+$, compute AUCell-like enrichment: $$\mathrm{AUC}_{k,+}=\sum_{r\le R} I\{g_r^{(k)}\in M_+\}\,w_r$$ Cells in the high quantile for $M_+$ and low quantile for opposite markers are Positive. |

## Practical comparison table

::: {.callout-note}
### Parameter grouping used in this table

- **Sparsity / regularization strength** groups parameters such as `alpha`, `alpha_2`, `ela_net_alpha`, and method-specific penalty controls.
- **Network / graph weighting** covers cell-cell, gene-gene, or community-structure regularization.
- **Cell-selection threshold** covers parameters such as `cutoff`, `tred`, `select_fraction`, `estimate_cutoff`, and quantile-like thresholds.
- **DE logFC threshold** merges `log2FC`, `Log2FC_cutoff`, and `logFC_threshold`.
- **DE p/FDR threshold** merges `p_adjust`, `pval_threshold`, `FDR_threshold`, and related significance cutoffs.
- Infrastructure-only parameters such as `seed`, `assay`, `tmp_dir`, cache paths, and low-level environment paths were intentionally excluded.
:::
